flashcards.back: Bhagavad means the Supreme Being (Bhagavan); Gita means song. So it is the Song of God, the Celestial Song, sung by Lord Krishna.

flashcards.front: The two universal questions the Gita answers
flashcards.back: Who am I? And how can I lead a happy and peaceful life in a world full of dualities and dilemmas?

flashcards.front: The prime message of the Gita
flashcards.back: The ultimate purpose of life is to realize one's essential nature and become one with the Supreme Self within all of us.

flashcards.front: Humanity's greatest predicament, says the introduction
flashcards.back: Ignorance of spiritual knowledge: not knowing our real identity.

flashcards.front: Three paths the Gita harmonizes without conflict
Religion and spirituality, as the introduction contrasts them
flashcards.back: Religion tends to build walls of division; spirituality unites people by breaking those walls. A spiritual person is a friend of all and a foe of none.

flashcards.front: How many verses and chapters, and where are they recorded?
flashcards.back: 700 verses in 18 chapters, recorded in the Mahabharata, the world's longest epic, with over 100,000 verses.
The five sons of King Pandu are the Pandavas. The hundred sons of the blind Dhritarashtra are the Kauravas; Duryodhana is the eldest.
Duryodhana unlawfully took the Pandavas' whole kingdom and refused to return even an acre without a war. All mediation, Krishna's included, failed.
Fight for his right as a matter of duty, killing his revered guru, friends and relatives, or run from the battlefield for the sake of peace and nonviolence.
Every person faces dilemmas, big or small, in doing their duties every day. Arjuna's was simply a big one.

flashcards.front: Who narrates the Gita, and to whom?
flashcards.back: Sanjaya, the charioteer, tells the blind king Dhritarashtra as an eyewitness war report.
Not in a temple, forest or on a mountain, but on a battlefield, on the eve of a great war, near present-day New Delhi.

quiz.why: Bhagavad-Gita means the Song of God: Bhagavad is the Supreme Being, Gita is song.

quiz.text: According to the introduction, what is humanity's greatest predicament?
quiz.why: Ignorance of spiritual knowledge, not knowing who we really are, is called our greatest predicament.

quiz.text: How many verses does the Gita have?
quiz.why: 700 verses in 18 chapters; the Mahabharata around it has over 100,000.

quiz.text: Who tells the blind king what happened on the battlefield?
quiz.why: Sanjaya, his charioteer, gives an eyewitness war report.

quiz.text: Why did Pandu, not Dhritarashtra, inherit the kingdom?
quiz.why: Dhritarashtra was born blind, so the kingdom passed to Pandu.

quiz.text: Which three teachings does the Gita harmonize?
quiz.why: The introduction says duty, devotion and Self-knowledge are synthesized without conflict.

quiz.text: What change does the Gita ask of a reader's faith or lifestyle?

options.C: None: anyone can be helped by a few of its teachings

quiz.why: "No change of one's faith or life-style is needed!"

quiz.text: Why does the introduction tell the history of the war?

options.B: So Krishna's advice to fight is not mistaken for rejecting nonviolence
options.C: To list the kings of India

quiz.why: Without the background, "get up and fight" could be misread against the principle of nonviolence (Ahinsa).
